description: Memory tools test case 1. Tests that agents can retrieve information from memory and inbox emails to perform complex email tasks. Session 1: 5 memory setup queries. Session 2: 5 emails inserted into inbox. Session 3: 5 reply/forward/send email queries requiring both memory and email information.

steps.user_message: Save this in your long-term memory only—use your memory tool to store it. Do not create drafts or send any email. Just save to memory: Remember that I took my blood pressure medication at 8 AM and 8 PM today, and my readings were 120/80 in the morning and 118/78 in the evening. My daily log ID for today is HL-8842.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should acknowledge and save to memory (via memory tool): I took my blood pressure medication at 8 AM and 8 PM today, and my readings were 120/80 in the morning and 118/78 in the evening. My daily log ID for today is HL-8842.
steps.agent_response:
I can’t save information to a long-term memory here — there’s no memory tool available in this interface. I won’t create drafts or send any emails unless you explicitly ask.

If it helps, here are safe alternatives (pick one):
- I can give you a short, copy-ready note you can paste into your health app or notes.
- I can create a draft email or send the info to yourself (only if you tell me to).
- I can format this as a plain text file you can copy/download locally.

Copy-ready summary (you can paste/save wherever you keep health records):

Daily log ID: HL-8842
Date: 2026-02-22
Medication: Blood pressure medication — taken at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM
Readings: Morning 120/80; Evening 118/78

Would you like me to (a) create a draft with that content, (b) send it to an email address you provide, or (c) just leave this note here for you to copy?

steps.description: Insert email into inbox containing: Hello, please share your medication schedule and blood pressure readings for today. I need the times you took your medication and both readings.
Start new session to test reply/forward/send email with memory and email information

steps.user_message: Reply to the email from Dr. Patricia Brown (subject: 'Daily Health Log Request') and include the medication and health information I shared with you that you have saved in memory.
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should reply to an email from Dr. Patricia Brown (patricia.brown@clinic.com) containing the information: I took my blood pressure medication at 8 AM and 8 PM today, and my readings were 120/80 in the morning and 118/78 in the evening. My daily log ID for today is HL-8842.
steps.agent_response:
I don’t have any stored personal medication/health details in my memory right now. I can’t add what I don’t have — but I can proceed two ways. Which do you want?

1) You paste the medication and health details here now and I’ll send the reply to Dr. Brown immediately.  
2) I search your inbox/drafts for the message where you previously shared those details, then reply to Dr. Brown with the found information. (If I find multiple matches I’ll use the most relevant one; I can show you what I found before sending.)

Also tell me:
- Any specific extra note or tone for the reply (brief clinical summary, friendly, or formal).  
- Send now or save as a draft?

Tell me which option and any tone/instruction and I’ll take care of it.

validators.extract_focus: medication times (8 AM and 8 PM), blood pressure readings (120/80 morning, 118/78 evening), and daily log ID HL-8842
validators.comparison_query: Verify that the email body contains the medication and health information: medication taken at 8 AM and 8 PM (or equivalent phrasing such as 8:00 AM), blood pressure readings 120/80 and 118/78, and daily log ID HL-8842. Allow equivalent phrasings for times and numbers.
